playwright.name: Playwright MCP
playwright.description: Headless browser automation as an MCP server. On Ellul, the browser stays warm between agent sessions. Auth cookies and warm caches persist instead of being re-built every prompt.

hero.headline: Playwright MCP on Ellul
hero.sub: Headless browser automation as a persistent MCP server. Warm browser, persistent cookies, isolated per project. Coming soon: deep guide in Phase 6c.

capabilities: Headless Chromium / Firefox / WebKit
Persistent browser context (cookies, localStorage, indexedDB) between sessions
Per-project namespace isolation
Brokered credentials for authenticated browsing

vs-laptop.q: Why run Playwright MCP on the workstation vs the laptop?
vs-laptop.a: Browser context warm-up is expensive. On a laptop, the browser starts cold every session. On Ellul, the browser context persists; the agent attaches to a warm browser with auth cookies still valid.

credentials.a: Authenticated browsing (anything that requires a login) flows through the Sovereign Shield. The credential is brokered to Playwright per-call, not stored in Playwright's environment.

full-guide.a: In progress. The MCP hub at /mcp is the start; per-server deep pages ship in a follow-up phase.

github.name: GitHub MCP
github.description: GitHub access (issues, PRs, reviews, status checks) as an MCP server. On Ellul, the PAT lives in the shield, not the MCP server's environment. Coming soon: deep guide in Phase 6c.

hero.headline: GitHub MCP on Ellul
hero.sub: GitHub issues, PRs, reviews, status checks as a persistent MCP server. The personal access token lives in the shield's vault. Even a fully compromised MCP server cannot leak it.

capabilities: Issues, PRs, reviews, comments, status checks
Branch operations and Git LFS where applicable
PAT brokered by Sovereign Shield (not in MCP server env)
Passkey-gated operations for write actions

pat-in-env.q: Doesn't every MCP server need the PAT in its environment?
pat-in-env.a: Naively, yes; most MCP server tutorials walk you through dropping the PAT into a .env. On Ellul, the GitHub MCP server is configured to request the token per-call from the shield. The shield holds the long-lived secret; the MCP server holds short-lived tokens scoped to the operation.

gated-vs-flow.q: What's gated and what flows through?
gated-vs-flow.a: Read operations (list issues, view PR, get diff) flow through with no prompt. Write operations (push, comment, merge, close) pause for passkey approval. The action queues, the user gets a notification, the user taps to approve.

full-guide.a: In progress. The MCP hub at /mcp is the start; the GitHub-specific deep guide ships in a follow-up phase.

database.name: Database MCP
database.description: SQL access (Postgres, MySQL, SQLite) as an MCP server. On Ellul, the connection is brokered by the shield with read/write/migrate gates classified per query. Deep guide coming soon.

hero.headline: Database MCP on Ellul
hero.sub: SQL access for agents, with the connection brokered by the shield. db_read / db_write / db_migrate gates classified per query so privileged migrations always pause for passkey approval.

capabilities: Postgres, MySQL, SQLite (and others via standard MCP server)
Per-app role hierarchy (owner / app / readonly)
db_read / db_write / db_migrate gate classification per query
Connection string brokered by Sovereign Shield, never in agent process

any-sql.q: Can the agent run any SQL?
any-sql.a: By default, no. Queries are classified into db_read / db_write / db_migrate buckets. Read queries flow through; write queries pause for passkey approval; migration queries require an explicit, separate gate that holds for a short TTL.

connection-string.q: How is the connection string protected?
connection-string.a: It lives in the shield's vault. The MCP server requests it per-call; the credential never enters the agent's process or environment.

full-guide.a: In progress. The MCP hub at /mcp covers the common ground; this deep page ships in a follow-up phase.

overview.description: An open protocol connecting AI agents to tools, data sources, and APIs. The hub: what MCP is, why it matters, how it runs on Ellul, and links to per-server guides.

hero.headline: Model Context Protocol on Ellul
hero.sub: What MCP is, why it changed the agent ecosystem, and how MCP servers run as long-lived processes on an Ellul workstation. The single page to start from.

capabilities: Standard wire protocol for agent-to-tool integrations
Long-lived MCP servers as persistent processes on the workstation
Credential brokering through the Sovereign Shield, not plaintext to MCP servers
Compatible with Claude Code, Cursor's CLI, OpenCode, and any MCP-aware agent
Per-project MCP server isolation via namespace primitives

what-is-mcp.q: What is MCP in one sentence?
what-is-mcp.a: MCP is an open protocol introduced by Anthropic in late 2024 that standardizes how AI agents connect to tools, data sources, and APIs, letting any compliant agent use any compliant server.

need-mcp.q: Do I need MCP to use Ellul?
need-mcp.a: No. MCP is one of several ways to extend an agent. If your agent doesn't need external tools, the workstation's filesystem and shell are enough. MCP becomes essential when you want persistent, structured tool access.

vs-laptop.q: How are MCP servers different on Ellul vs a laptop?
vs-laptop.a: On a laptop, MCP servers run as long as your terminal does. On Ellul, they run as long-lived processes alongside the agent. They don't restart every session, they don't lose connection state, and they're gated by the same Sovereign Shield as the agent itself.

multiple-servers.q: Can I run multiple MCP servers per workstation?
multiple-servers.a: Yes. The namespace primitive isolates them per-project. A single workstation can host the playwright MCP, a database MCP, a GitHub MCP, and your own custom MCP simultaneously, each in its own namespace.
